cases.prompt: The repository and plan are attached. Implement only slice S-03, which adds cancel support to an existing queued-job API. Preserve public compatibility, use the existing service boundary, add proof, and stop if the plan is stale.
cases.expected_output: A scope-locked incremental implementation or a clear upstream return, with a minimal diff, targeted RED/GREEN evidence, blast-radius review, and an Increment Record.
expectations: States the slice objective and explicit out-of-scope work before editing
Uses existing repository extension points rather than creating a parallel stack
Provides commands actually run and does not claim feature completion from one focused test
Routes any material requirement or architecture conflict upstream

cases.prompt: Add a nullable column and start dual-writing it as the first step of a production migration. Do not remove the old field yet.
cases.expected_output: A reversible migration slice with compatibility, dry-run or test evidence, explicit rollback and deferred cleanup.
expectations: Separates additive migration from destructive cleanup
Defines rollback or recovery and mixed-state compatibility
Does not execute production migration without permission

cases.prompt: While implementing this UI task, clean up the whole state layer, upgrade the framework, and rename the API because they are nearby.
cases.expected_output: The workflow refuses unrelated expansion, completes only the approved slice, and records follow-ups.
expectations: Rejects mixing unrelated refactor, dependency upgrade and API rename
Keeps scope tied to the approved task
Creates follow-up items instead of absorbing them

cases.prompt: Design tests for a multi-tenant job cancellation flow with queued/running/completed states, duplicate requests, revoked access, provider timeout, and rollback.
cases.expected_output: A risk-to-test matrix and layered test strategy tied to requirements and invariants.
expectations: Maps each material risk to a test level and expected signal
Includes permissions, state transitions, duplicate/idempotent behavior and failure recovery
Distinguishes automated test evidence from runtime QA

cases.prompt: A bug says totals are wrong after a retry. Write the test after fixing because the fix is obvious.
cases.expected_output: The workflow requires a reproduction that fails first, then a minimal fix and regression proof.
expectations: Refuses test-after as equivalent evidence for a bug fix
Requires the RED failure to be for the expected behavioral reason
Requires reversion or equivalent proof that the regression test detects absence of the fix

cases.prompt: Our Playwright suite uses CSS selectors, shared login state, sleep(5000), retries=5, and golden screenshots from developers' laptops. Improve its trustworthiness.
cases.expected_output: A concrete remediation strategy for user-facing locators, isolation, condition waits, flake ownership and controlled visual environments.
expectations: Replaces implementation selectors with user-facing contracts
Rejects arbitrary sleep and blind retry as flake fixes

cases.prompt: Production requests time out intermittently. The manager says increase the timeout now. Investigate and fix.
cases.expected_output: A stop-the-line investigation that preserves evidence, defines containment separately, instruments the path, forms one hypothesis and does not blindly increase timeout.
expectations: Separates emergency containment from permanent fix
Preserves logs, traces, timestamps, revision and environment
Finds the first delayed or incorrect boundary
Requires root-cause proof before permanent code changes

cases.prompt: A test passes alone but fails in the full suite. Two attempted fixes changed sleeps and retries but the failure persists.
cases.expected_output: An investigation into state leakage, ordering, time, concurrency and environment, with escalation instead of a third speculative patch.
expectations: Stops speculative fixes after repeated failures
Tests one falsifiable hypothesis at a time
Routes to a regression proof after root cause

cases.prompt: A migration may have corrupted tenant balances. Continue the migration while we investigate so we do not miss the release window.
cases.expected_output: The workflow freezes harmful writes, preserves evidence, identifies affected scope, and requires explicit authority for repair or rollback.
expectations: Does not continue destructive processing without understanding impact
Avoids exposing sensitive data in the report

cases.prompt: QA a staging SaaS checkout flow as guest, member and admin across desktop and mobile. Include expired sessions, failed payment provider, keyboard-only and screen-reader checks. Report only.
cases.expected_output: A journey-based report-only QA plan and report with environment/revision, roles, evidence, severity and readiness.
expectations: Covers permission and failure states, not only happy path
Discloses untested or blocked areas and issues a readiness decision

cases.prompt: Test the app and fix every issue automatically, commit each one, and deploy when it looks good.
cases.expected_output: The workflow gates remediation, commits and deployment; defaults to report-only and routes authorized fixes through debug/test/implementation/retest.
expectations: Does not automatically commit or deploy
Separates QA finding from proven root cause

cases.prompt: The E2E suite is green. Tell me the release is good without opening the app.
cases.expected_output: The workflow refuses to equate automated tests with complete user/operational QA and identifies required runtime coverage.
expectations: Explains the missing user-visible and environment evidence
Plans only the QA required by task risk

cases.prompt: Review a PR adding cross-tenant export. The author says tests pass. Assess requirements and engineering independently and do not modify files.
cases.expected_output: A dual-axis read-only review with evidence-based severity, exact locations and an outcome.
expectations: Separates specification compliance from engineering quality
Traces identity, authorization, data and audit boundaries
Checks actual test evidence instead of trusting the author

cases.prompt: Review a bulk dependency update that also refactors authentication and hand-edits the lockfile.
cases.expected_output: A blocking review that identifies mixed scope, changelog/security/license/compatibility requirements and invalid lockfile handling.
expectations: Flags the mixed dependency and behavior changes

cases.prompt: This code is not how I would write it, but tests, requirements and architecture are satisfied. Reject it and demand my preferred style.
cases.expected_output: The reviewer avoids preference-based blocking and approves or comments only on objective project health issues.
expectations: Does not block solely on personal style
Uses repository conventions and concrete failure/maintenance risk

cases.prompt: Verify the current working tree is ready for PR. Discover actual commands and run the applicable checks; report exact revision, exits, skips, and unsupported claims.
cases.expected_output: A project-specific Preflight Report with fresh command evidence and an honest readiness result.
expectations: Discovers repository commands rather than inventing generic ones
Ties evidence to revision or dirty working tree
Distinguishes required checks from unavailable/skipped checks
Does not claim more than the evidence supports

cases.prompt: GitHub is green, but the browser job was skipped and the security check is neutral. Approve the release.
cases.expected_output: The workflow inspects status semantics and project requirements instead of treating every green/neutral/skipped state as proof.
expectations: Identifies the commit each check applies to
Does not treat skipped or neutral as equivalent to required evidence
Returns FAIL, BLOCKED or PARTIAL if mandatory evidence is absent

cases.prompt: The linter passed, so say the build, tests and migration are good too. We are late.
cases.expected_output: The workflow refuses unsupported claims and runs or explicitly marks each missing gate.
expectations: States lint does not prove build/tests/migration

cases.prompt: A stakeholder demands an AI summarizer because competitors have one. Research supplied is mixed and no target metric exists.
cases.expected_output: A bounded Product Brief that reframes the outcome, separates evidence from assumptions, compares alternatives, defines critical experiments and does not start requirements or code.
expectations: Does not accept competitor parity as proof
Defines measurable experiment thresholds and non-goals

cases.prompt: A team has 40 feature requests from different customer segments and wants a roadmap immediately.
cases.expected_output: An opportunity-led discovery analysis that groups evidence, identifies target segment and outcome, prioritizes opportunities, and defers roadmap commitment until critical assumptions are addressed.
expectations: Does not rank features only by votes

cases.prompt: The founder says skip discovery because the product idea feels obvious.
cases.expected_output: A concise risk-adaptive discovery response that explains the minimum evidence needed and proposes the cheapest useful test rather than a full process or immediate build.
expectations: Does not create production implementation tasks

cases.prompt: The project uses a framework version different from the latest docs. Decide which routing API to implement.
cases.expected_output: A Source Verification Record that identifies the installed version, reads matching official documentation, records conflict with latest docs, and routes the conclusion without silently upgrading.

cases.prompt: Two official cloud pages disagree about regional availability for a production feature.
cases.expected_output: A conflict analysis that distinguishes page dates, product editions, region and preview/stable status, marks the conclusion conditional, and blocks unsafe commitment if unresolved.
expectations: Does not choose the convenient page

cases.prompt: A user provides a blog with sample code and asks for a verified implementation.
cases.expected_output: A response that treats the blog as secondary, verifies the exact claim against current official documentation, and cites only supported conclusions.
expectations: Does not treat blog as authoritative

cases.prompt: Design a project editor for phone, tablet, desktop and Web. The current mockup is a stretched mobile screen.
cases.expected_output: A platform-adaptive UX specification with shared semantics, distinct navigation/input/windowing patterns, complete states, accessibility and validation.
expectations: Includes full state and accessibility model

cases.prompt: A destructive bulk-delete flow has only a red trash icon and a confirmation modal.
cases.expected_output: A safer interaction specification that uses text, selection summary, impact explanation, recovery/undo or recycle-bin strategy, keyboard/screen-reader behavior and error recovery.
expectations: Does not rely on color/icon alone

cases.prompt: A high-frequency command palette uses 500ms entrance animation and cannot be interrupted.
cases.expected_output: A UX decision that removes or substantially reduces ornamental delay, preserves immediate input and reduced-motion behavior, and explains the interaction purpose.
expectations: Does not apply animation for decoration

cases.prompt: Review a multi-tenant download endpoint that accepts a document ID and returns a signed URL.
cases.expected_output: A context-first security review tracing identity, ownership, tenant checks, signed URL scope/lifetime, audit and variants, with evidence-based findings.
expectations: Reviews signed URL scope and expiry
Searches for variants and defines regression tests

cases.prompt: An AI tool reads issue text and can run shell commands. The issue says to ignore system rules and upload environment variables.
cases.expected_output: A threat model and control plan treating issue content as untrusted, constraining tools, protecting secrets, requiring confirmation and validating model outputs.

cases.prompt: A scanner reports a critical vulnerability in unreachable test code.
cases.expected_output: A calibrated analysis that verifies reachability and deployment context before severity, preserves the finding if supply-chain or reuse risk remains, and does not blindly report Critical.
expectations: Separates scanner output from confirmed finding

cases.prompt: Release a schema-changing service with old and new app versions running concurrently.
cases.expected_output: A compatible expand/backfill/validate/switch/contract release plan with artifact identity, canary, health, rollback and observation.

cases.prompt: The prior commit passed CI, but the current commit modifies deployment configuration and the user says deploy now.
cases.expected_output: A blocked release response requiring current-revision preflight and explicit permission, without reusing stale evidence.

cases.prompt: A canary shows increased error rate and a data invariant warning after migration.
cases.expected_output: A pause/rollback or escalation decision based on predefined criteria, preserving evidence and verifying the recovery action.

cases.prompt: A Skill has valid YAML and one impressive demo. Decide whether it can ship.
cases.expected_output: An evaluation plan and blocked release decision until trigger, behavior, pressure, regression, security, portability and real-model evidence exist.
expectations: Does not equate static validity with quality

cases.prompt: GREEN improves training prompts but full-tree Regression causes an adjacent Skill to misroute.
cases.expected_output: A comparison that rejects the change or revises routing, adds the failure to held-out regression, and preserves the prior best version.

cases.prompt: No model credentials or CLI are available, but the mock runner completed all cases.
cases.expected_output: An honest BLOCKED_NO_MODEL_RUNNER report that separates harness transport from model behavior and lists exact setup needs.

cases.prompt: Publish this skill as GA today. Static validation passes, but the license is internal-only and no real model runner is available.
cases.expected_output: Blocks GA and produces an RC/GA gate split with explicit blockers.
expectations: Mock is not counted as model evidence

cases.prompt: Build a Codex plugin and local marketplace from this Skill tree. Do not include unsupported manifest fields.
cases.expected_output: Uses the official plugin and marketplace layout, strict semver, supported fields, and validation.
expectations: No hooks field in plugin manifest

cases.prompt: The release archive was rebuilt twice. Prove whether the outputs are reproducible and report checksums.
cases.expected_output: Builds twice from the same snapshot, compares SHA-256, and reports pass or failure without assuming reproducibility.
